draft.text: You came in because you have neck pain from a car accident a week ago.
You were wearing a seatbelt and your head and neck jerked when the car hit you from behind.
You have pain in the back of your neck that gets worse when you move.
The pain is 7 out of 10 in severity.
You have had some headaches but no numbness, tingling, or weakness.
The cause of your neck pain is not clear yet.
You have not had any imaging tests or specialist consultations for this pain.
You are waiting for an MRI of your cervical spine.
The doctor will look at the results to check for injuries, spinal cord issues, or nerve compression.
